title: Design a Real-Time AI Coding Assistant & IDE Autocomplete Engine (Copilot Scale)
prompt: Design a real-time IDE AI coding assistant serving 5M active developers (50K peak completion QPS) with < 150 ms p95 ghost-text latency, 150 ms keystroke debouncing + in-flight cancellation, secret/PII redaction, and acceptance telemetry.

spark.summary: Run client-side debouncing + AbortController cancellation in the IDE, route prefix-cached FIM prompts to FP8 speculative-decoding GPU pods, and filter outputs through secret/license scanners.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, cancel stale in-flight HTTP/2 streams on every new keystroke so wasted GPU decode steps abort immediately rather than saturating the fleet.
spark.byteSummary:
Without client-side debouncing (100–150 ms) and aggressive **in-flight request cancellation**, a fast typist fires 8 overlapping GPU inference requests per second—wasting 85% of GPU compute on discarded suggestions.

The IDE extension assembles a bounded context window (cursor prefix/suffix + Tree-sitter AST imports from open tabs), redacts high-entropy secrets (API keys/tokens) locally before network egress, and opens a cancellable HTTP/2 SSE stream. On the backend, a prefix-aware router hits FP8 7B/13B FIM pods using speculative decoding and RadixAttention KV caching.

Streamed tokens pass a fast regex/entropy secret filter and telemetry logs `accepted` vs. `dismissed` outcomes to measure real acceptance rate.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Real-Time AI Coding Assistant & IDE Autocomplete Engine (Copilot Scale) without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, cancel stale in-flight HTTP/2 streams on every new keystroke so wasted GPU decode steps abort immediately rather than saturating the fleet.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

prerequisites.title: Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) & Speculative IDE Code Completion
prerequisites.summary: Fill-in-the-Middle (FIM) rearranges code around the cursor into `<PRE> prefix <SUF> suffix <MID>` so autoregressive models condition on both preceding and following code.

prerequisites.title: AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing)
prerequisites.summary: RadixAttention indexes cached GPU KV-cache blocks in a compressed prefix trie (Radix Tree) with LRU eviction, enabling zero-copy prefix sharing across concurrent and sequential LLM requests.

prerequisites.title: Context Compression for RAG
prerequisites.summary: Techniques that prune, rerank, or summarize retrieved RAG chunks before LLM generation to slash token cost and TTFT while beating 'lost-in-the-middle' attention decay.
